sections.what: Brighter Bites distributes fresh produce to families through schools and community partners. Nutrition education and cooking demonstrations help children and caregivers use that produce. Its Houston program is part of a broader multiregional nonprofit.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 annual impact report records 264,354 students, teachers and families impacted, not unique households. It reports a 40% SNAP-Ed funding loss and the closure of Austin in December 2025. Houston's 2024–2025 school locations are published, but we did not verify an annual Houston household cohort or local budget. Current descriptions of 20-pound weekly bags differ from the original return's 25-pound, 50-serving description. The 2025 Cambridge paper uses three Houston focus groups conducted in 2022, with single-group purposive and convenience sampling. Participants described buying new produce; the study does not establish controlled clinical or expenditure effects. Useful follow-up would include distinct households, pickup frequency, geographic budgets, causal health effects and actual cash expenditure.
sections.qualitative: Recurring distribution combines food access with practical preparation skills. Houston schools and food-bank partners provide an established delivery network. Published research examines dietary behaviors and family shopping mechanisms. Mixed counts of students, teachers and families do not identify unique annual households. Dietary behavior studies and focus groups do not measure clinical QALYs or causal net cash gains. National costs, Houston allocations, funding cuts and donated resources require careful boundaries. The original IRS return identifies Brighter Bites, EIN 47-4070026, headquartered in Houston. The current Houston page lists local partners, schools and donation links. The official donation page embeds Blackbaud. No transaction was performed.
sections.cost: Our conditional reference is approximately $88.83 million per better life: ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents. It combines 0.992638 clinical QALYs with 0.825477 signed income/consumption equivalents. The denominator is the full national annual recognized cost of $16,150,774; only a hypothetical Houston nutrition and household-resource channel enters the benefit numerator. This is not a matched Houston program cost, complete organization expected value, restricted-gift price or demonstrated next-dollar return. A proportional $10,000 share corresponds to approximately 0.001126 combined equivalents under this accounting hypothesis, not proven marginal expansion. We use 25,000 national annual family opportunities and 0.8 distinct-household mapping as explicit unsupported judgments, not a conversion of the mixed 264,354-person count. Additional annual response of 0.5, relative to food banks, SNAP, school meals and existing purchases, leaves 10,000 household proxies. One child per household supplies the clinical proxy: response 0.3, utility improvement 0.01 for half a year, and full union harm of 0.001. These are nutrition hypotheses, not measured mortality or QALY effects. A judged Houston share of 0.2 is applied once to health and resources; we have not verified the geographic allocation. Half of exposed households are assumed to avoid $200 of otherwise-paid food costs after benefits and replacement support. A 0.5 positive-only overlap discount precedes the full $25 pickup, preparation and foregone-time burden, leaving $75 for successful households and −$25 for the others. Resources use one adult consumption-equivalent per household at a $30,000 annual baseline, with components netted before one logarithm. Increased produce purchases can raise spending; adverse cases retain negative gains, full costs and union harms. Retail bag value, donated-produce valuation, gross wages and property wealth are not added. Food-bank inputs, volunteer time, public funding and other provider opportunity costs remain unknown centrally; higher-cost and payer/provider-loss cases test their incidence. Benefits outside Houston and from other programs are omitted from this partial-channel reference, not judged zero.
sections.funding: The original FY2024 functional expense is $15,948,524. Adding $202,250 of direct event expenses netted from revenue gives $16,150,774. FY2023 is $15,132,611 plus $20,814, or $15,153,425; FY2022 is $15,514,468 plus $188,812, or $15,703,280. The FY2025 impact report's unaudited financial table reports $16,383,946 of expenses, including $6,883,080 in kind. We have not verified that figure as an event-inclusive denominator or complete social cost, so it remains financial-vintage context rather than the central cost. The latest index also flags FY2025 audit control issues that need further review. The current $350-per-family annual solicitation is not a measured next-gift price.

model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
